evidence.quote:
2
A claimant is entitled to state pension credit if—
a
he is in Great Britain;
b
he has attained the qualifying age; and
c
he satisfies—
i
the condition in section 2(1) (guarantee credit); or
ii
the conditions in section 3(1) and (2) (savings credit).

claims.scope_or_qualification: This is an unreviewed machine extraction requested for 20 September 2026, with observed extent E+W+S. Commencement, contemporary applicability, complete amendments and the referenced component conditions in sections 2 and 3 are not established by the package.
claims.statement: The selected statutory extraction states that entitlement requires the claimant to be in Great Britain, have attained the qualifying age, and satisfy either the Guarantee Credit condition or the Savings Credit conditions.

evidence.quote:
77031 A claimant is entitled to SPC if they1


1. are in GB and


2. have reached the qualifying age and


3. satisfy the conditions to get a GC or SC and


4. are not a member of a


      4.1 couple where the other member is entitled to SPC or


      4.2 mixed-age couple (see DMG 77035 and 77140)


      4.3 polygamous marriage (see DMG 77016) where the other party to the marriage or the additional
      spouse are members of the same household and entitled to SPC (but see DMG 77140 et seq) and


5. have made a valid claim2 and


6. where relevant, their partner, satisfy the NI provisions (see DMG Chapter 02) 3.

claims.scope_or_qualification: This is frozen, unreviewed DMG guidance rather than current-law assurance. The referenced continuations—including DMG 77016, 77140 onwards and Chapter 02—are not supplied completely. The conditions distinguish claimant and partner status and do not establish payment amount.
claims.statement: The selected DMG page presents additional general conditions: the claimant must not fall within specified couple, mixed-age-couple or polygamous-marriage exclusions, must make a valid claim and, where relevant, the partner must satisfy National Insurance provisions.

evidence.quote:
Mixed-age couple

77035 For the purposes of entitlement to SPC, a mixed-age couple is one where one member has

reached the qualifying age and the other has not.1 This definition includes a polygamous marriage where
at least one party to the polygamous marriage has reached the qualifying age and at least one party has
not2.


Note 1: This definition applies only to new claims to SPC from 15.5.19. Savings provisions have effect as

though the exclusion of mixed-age couples from SPC had not come into force 2. So a member of a mixed-
age couple who was entitled to SPC or pension age HB or both on 14.5.19, continues to be so entitled on
or after 15.5.19. The savings provisions cease to have effect to a member of a mixed-age couple on or
after 15.5.19 when that person is no longer entitled to SPC or pension age HB as part of the same mixed-
age couple.

claims.scope_or_qualification: The protection is tied to the stated household composition, entitlement on 14 May 2019 and uninterrupted entitlement as the same mixed-age couple. Detailed guidance at DMG 77140 onwards, later migration provisions and current applicability remain unresolved.
claims.statement: For a mixed-age couple, the selected guidance defines the category and describes a dated continuity protection for certain existing awards, rather than a general exception for every mixed-age couple.

summary: The truncated package supports only a partial, frozen-source account. It indicates that State Pension Credit generally requires presence in Great Britain, qualifying age and satisfaction of the conditions for Guarantee Credit or Savings Credit; the guidance also identifies a valid claim and, where relevant, National Insurance provisions. Mixed-age couples are subject to dated exclusions and continuity protections. The package does not establish complete current entitlement conditions, territorial and transitional rules, claim requirements or credit-specific financial tests, so it cannot determine whether any citizen qualifies.
